facts.text: The action space is Discrete(2): the only valid actions are the integers 0 and 1
Action 1 applies a push of +force_mag and any other valid action applies -force_mag
The model constants are gravity 9.8, cart mass 1.0, pole mass 0.1, pole half-length 0.5, force magnitude 10.0, integration step 0.02 s and the euler integrator
The episode fails when the pole angle leaves 12 degrees or the cart position leaves 2.4
The observation bounds are twice the failure thresholds: cart position +-4.8, pole angle about +-0.418 rad, and the two velocity bounds are the float32 maximum
The observation has four elements: cart position, cart velocity, pole angle and pole angular velocity
step returns the state as a float32 numpy array
The episode terminates when the cart position or the pole angle crosses its threshold
The constructor's sutton_barto_reward default is False

When sutton_barto_reward is False every step pays 1.0, including the terminating step, and 0.0 after the episode; when it is True a non-terminal step pays 0.0 and a terminal or post-terminal step pays -1.0
CartPoleEnv.step always reports truncated=False; the episode length limit is the TimeLimit wrapper that make() adds
reset() accepts options and uses the default bounds -0.05 and 0.05; it draws the four state values uniformly between low and high
The model is a cart on a frictionless track with an un-actuated pole joint; an action is a fixed-magnitude push

determinism.notes: reset(seed=...) and cap.world.seed.v1 fix the next reset, and the dynamics are deterministic, so one implementation repeats a trajectory for the same seed and actions; the fake draws initial states with Python's random.Random while upstream draws them with numpy's generator, so the same seed need not give the same trajectory on the fake and upstream

gaps: frictionless point-mass cart-pole with an un-actuated joint: no contacts, friction, actuator dynamics, sensor model or measurement noise; the push is an ideal fixed-magnitude force
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, so ticks advance simulated time by timestep_ms only
no physical device is modelled and the model was not validated against one

the fake backend is a pure Python re-implementation using random.Random and Python floats instead of numpy's generator and float32 arrays; it was not compared with the upstream environment, and robust_gymnasium was not installed where the gate ran
the bridge's unlisted sim backend calls gymnasium.make('CartPole-v1'), i.e. the base Gymnasium distribution, not robust_gymnasium.make; only the package fake is provided and checked
snapshot and restore are not offered: CartPoleEnv exposes no get_state/set_state

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulator stops advancing: after an e-stop no reset or step is accepted until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch, while the last observation stays readable
